## Purpose
[Anonymized Customer] Novus Project will implement a single Oracle SaaS platform for Finance and Supply Chain across the [Anonymized Customer] Group. The purpose of this document is to provide a High-Level Global Design for the Novus Project. “Global” shall mean a single common system design for the Oracle Cloud applications, for adoption by Group Entities in all regions. “Localizations” shall mean parts of the design that are local to a specific site for local statutory or legal reasons. The relationship of this document to other items within the whole end-to-end solution of the Novus Project can be summarized in the Enterprise Architecture context diagram below. This document should be taken as a Master Document for referring to detailed design documents that constitute the whole design. Additional supporting documents should be referenced in Appendix A. This document has been created to deliver the Global Design for all [Anonymized Customer] legal entities based on the Novus project design principles and adopting an Oracle Cloud SaaS solution at the time of the Global Design and validation phases of the Novus project. Following the implementation of the pilot sites in the Benelux Sales Channels and DLG Manufacturing, during the rollout to other [Anonymized Customer] entities, design decisions and processes may evolve whether globally or have local exceptions. In additional new release features and Oracle cloud services, licensed not yet implemented, may be deployed.

heading: ## Design Principles
chunk:
## Design Principles
The Novus project design principles the global design aligns to are:
---
**Table:**
| 1 | Process harmonization | Process harmonization is a key driver. Wherever possible, we need to agree consistent processes and policies for all activities. |
| 2 | Customer Experience | One process, with little exceptions. This brings consistency of our customers and customer facing teams. We need to modernize our systems for a superior customer life-time experience. |
| 3 | Simplify and streamline | Strive for a seamless process We need to breakdown ‘walls’ between our systems. Leverage features from our new business system tools to allow for value-add activities. |
| 4 | Adopt system defined processes | Adopt system-defined processes to align with best practice where possible. We need to avoid processes that drive system customizations. |
| 5 | Avoid working outside of core systems | We need to eliminate spreadsheets and manual work whenever possible. |
| 6 | Automate processes | Starts with proper design and has the customer in mind. We must get to a point where we understand the complete end-to-end process and mitigate weak points. |
| 7 | Do it once, do it right | Reduce the number of human driven choices. We must enforce data discipline and drive data quality. |
| 8 | Consider the user experience | Allow self-service on a device and at time that suits them. We need to consider how users’ interface with [Anonymized Customer] through our business systems. |

heading: ## Application Security
chunk:
## Application Security
Oracle ERP Cloud application security will be applied to each user / system account. A user account in Identity Management will be associated with a single employee record in Oracle HCM. Oracle ERP Cloud application security separates functional security (what the user can do) from data security (what the user can see). Therefore, role-based access control (RBAC) has two components for each Role: The Job Role and the Data Role. The first restricts access to specific functions (Job Role), and the second restricts access to the data that can be retrieved through the application (Data Role). Users will be assigned specific role(s) which control what they can do, and what they can view. Where custom roles have been created, these are documented in a separate configuration workbook. See Appendix A for links to the Configuration Workbooks.
